💿 How to get a song
1. In Spotify, tap Share → Copy link on the song to copy its link.
2. Open the built-in converter below (🎵 Spotify to MP3 / WAV / FLAC), paste the link and tap Convert.
3. Tap ⬇ Download or Import to Library — the file keeps its title, artist, album and cover art, and stays on your device.
💡 Backup: if the in-app converter can't find the song
These open your link pre-filled — convert there, download the MP3, then import it with + Add songs → + Files:
Spotisaver SpotMate
🎛️ Conversion Tools Spotify · YouTube · MP4 · Expand URL
🔗 Expand URL
Paste a short Spotify link (open.spotify.com/s/...) to get the full track URL for converters. Note: If you already have the full open.spotify.com/track/... URL you don't need this step — it's just a fallback for short links.
🎵 Spotify to MP3 / WAV / FLAC
⚠ Experimental — Paste a Spotify song, album or playlist link below, pick your format (MP3, WAV or FLAC), and convert — done right in the app. Albums and playlists resolve their real track list, then you choose whether each song saves on its own or everything lands in one ZIP — every file keeps its real name, artist and cover. Note: WAV/FLAC are lossless (higher quality) but take up far more storage than MP3 — roughly 5–10× the size. MP3 is plenty for most listening.
🎬 YouTube to MP3
⚠ Experimental — Paste any YouTube URL, pick MP3, WAV or FLAC, and convert. If your format can't be produced, it falls back to another one automatically.
🎞️ MP4 to WAV / FLAC / MP3 Converter
⚠ Experimental — Convert MP4 video files to WAV, FLAC, or MP3 audio directly in your browser. No upload needed, everything stays on your device.
💡 Audio formats explained
MP3 — the everyday format. Compressed, small files (about 1 MB/minute), sounds great on most speakers/headphones. Best for phone/device storage.
WAV — lossless, uncompressed. The highest quality but huge — roughly 10 MB/minute (5–10× an MP3). Best when quality matters more than space (editing, archival, hi-fi).
M4A / AAC — Apple/iTunes's compressed format. Same idea as MP3, often slightly better quality at the same size.
FLAC — lossless but much smaller than WAV (~5 MB/minute) while keeping all the detail. Great middle ground if your device plays it.
OGG / Opus — very efficient modern format; best compression for the same quality.
Rule of thumb: if you're just listening, MP3 is more than enough and keeps your library small. Only pick WAV/FLAC when you want lossless and have plenty of storage.

The whole tutorial in text:
•Getting music in: SideCut plays audio files saved on your device. The free way: Spotify → Share → Copy link → paste into Expand URL → take the full link to any Spotify-to-MP3 converter → import the MP3s with + Add songs ▾ → + Files. + Add folder grabs a whole folder; Import library restores a backup .zip.
•Playing: tap any song to play it; use the mini player at the bottom for play/pause, skip, and shuffle. Tap the ⋮ next to a song for more options.
•Jump to the playing song: tap the record on the now bar. In Playlists it scrolls straight to that song in the list (switching to All Songs only if the open playlist does not hold it); in Albums it opens the album the song is in, scrolled to it and highlighted.
•Albums: the Albums tab and the “Add to album” picker show only the albums you made. To build one: long-press a row to select songs (from anywhere), then use the album + or album-with-arrow button in the header. Hold a song 3 seconds inside an album to reorder it; Done keeps, Cancel restores.
•Stats: a play counts only after you pass the halfway point of a track, or it finishes — skipping through songs doesn't count. The same rule feeds most played, top artists and total plays.
•Updates: you don't have to look for them. A new build is announced on the next launch and parked in the 🔔 bell as ⬆ Update available with Install now; installing waits for a playing song to finish instead of cutting it. Manual path: Settings → More → Check for updates.
•Scenario — backup / new phone: Export everything → one .zip (songs, covers, playlists, albums, tags, stats; 2–3 minutes for 500 songs). New phone: Import library → pick the .zip. “Export songs only” is audio-only.
•Look: Settings → Theme for looks, Glow for edge lines and glow, Playback for crossfade/gapless, Equalizer for 8-band EQ.
•Organizing: create playlists from the Playlists tab, add songs via the ⋮ menu, long-press a row to select multiple tracks, and Export library to back everything up as a .zip.
•Notifications: the media player in your phone\'s notification shade plays/pauses but tapping it won\'t open SideCut — open the app manually to get back to the song list.
Works offline
Once your songs are imported, SideCut keeps running with no connection:
Yes — playing your library, playlists, shuffle/repeat, EQ, DJ mode, seek, sleep timer, gapless, crossfade, lyrics you've already fetched, all saved settings, and every Sandbox tweak (custom quick actions, Home layout).
Needs internet — Discover (song search, previews, pinned artists, new-release checks), fetching new lyrics or covers, and update checks. Your actual music files always play straight from this device.
Need help? Try the 🤖 AI Assistant in Settings → Support — it knows everything about SideCut and works instantly offline. If the AI can't help, contact us at sidecutsupport@gmail.com (Settings → Support).
Accepted file types
Audio: .mp3, .m4a, .wav, .flac, .ogg, .aac, .wma, .opus, .aiff, .alac
Other: .zip (library/playlist import), .csv (Spotify playlist import)
Read this before using SideCut.
SideCut has themes, glow effects, and an RGB color mode that produce flashing, pulsing, and rapidly changing colors — including along the edges of your screen while music plays.
A very small number of people may experience seizures or loss of consciousness when exposed to certain flashing lights or patterns, even with no history of seizures or epilepsy.
If you have photosensitive epilepsy, or have ever had a seizure triggered by flashing lights, turn these effects off:
•Avoid the RGB, RGB+, and animated dynamic themes (Aurora, Synthwave, Ocean, Ember, Galaxy, Cyberpunk, Glacier).
•In Glow settings, leave the edge lines, blur bands, and corner glow off.
•Use a static theme (Rose Gold, Violet, Onyx, etc.) and the DJ Mode visuals with caution.
•Sandbox → Reduce motion disables all animations and transitions across the app.
Stop using the app and consult a doctor if you experience dizziness, altered vision, eye or muscle twitching, loss of awareness, or disorientation while using it. Keep a safe distance from the screen and play in a well-lit room.

Enabled
Rolling back swaps the app to a saved copy of an older version that lives as a separate, self-contained snapshot on this device — the actual SideCut app installed on your device (and its cached shell) stays exactly as it is; only what this tab shows changes. Your library and settings live in their own storage, untouched by the switch.
⚠ Before you roll back
Older versions can have side effects: data loss or a broken app that won\'t open or run correctly. If that happens you'll need to clear app data to recover, which wipes your library. Back up your library first — use Export library to save a .zip you can restore after clearing data. Don't roll back without a backup.

Understanding the version numbers
Turn DJ Mode off for any individual playlist — handy for religious or devotional playlists you'd rather listen to as-is. Built-in names (Paath, Gurbani, Kirtaan, Dhadi Jhatta, Gurmukhi, Religious, Prayer) are always off and shown locked below.
A few built-in behaviors worth knowing:
•Hold the mini record player to adjust its angle. Long-press the little turntable at the bottom of the screen — a Turntable angle popup opens with TILT / SPIN / ROLL sliders. Drag them while the preview moves live; Reset brings back the default look. A quick tap still jumps to the playing song.
•DJ Mode is disabled for certain playlists. If a playlist is named Paath, Gurbani, Kirtaan, Dhadi Jhatta, Gurmukhi, Religious, or Prayer — uppercase or lowercase, it doesn't matter — DJ Mode steps aside for that playlist. You can also turn DJ Mode off manually for any playlist from DJ Mode per playlist above — handy for religious or devotional playlists you'd rather listen to as-is. You'll see a small note when this happens.
•Your music stays on your device. SideCut plays files you import — it never uploads them. Fetching new lyrics or covers, and update checks, are the only things that need internet.
•Update timestamps are in Eastern time (EDT). Every changelog entry shows its date and time in Eastern time — never UTC, and never the build machine's clock.
•Jump to the playing song from anywhere. Tap the record on the now bar — in Playlists it scrolls to that song in the list, in Albums it opens the album it is in. Either way the row is highlighted so you never have to hunt for it.
•The phone's media player can't open SideCut. The notification-shade / lock-screen player can play, pause, and skip — but tapping it won\'t open the app. To get back to the song list, open SideCut from your launcher.
•Lyrics auto-scroll isn't perfect. Timed lyrics are matched to a best-effort sync, so the highlight can drift — tap Auto-scroll in the lyrics view to turn it off and read at your own pace.
•Back up before rolling back. Older app versions can break things or lose data. Use Export library to save a .zip first, since recovering from a bad rollback may require clearing app data.

How to use SideCut

Getting music into your library
SideCut plays audio files saved on your device — it doesn't stream or fetch anything itself. The free way to get a song from Spotify (no premium needed):
1.In Spotify, tap Share → Copy link on any song to copy the short link.
2.Paste it into Expand URL (Settings → Expand URL, or the box at the top of Discover) — it becomes the full track URL that converters accept. (Already have the full URL? You can skip this, but it’s handy if Spotify changes their link format.)
3.Paste the expanded URL into any Spotify-to-MP3 converter and download the file.
4.Back in SideCut, tap + Add songs ▾ → + Files and pick the downloaded MP3s — they're now stored locally on your device.
•+ Add folder grabs a whole folder at once — handy for a full album or your Downloads folder
•Import library restores a full backup .zip, including playlists and tags
Playing music
•Tap any song in your list to start playing it
•Use the mini player at the bottom for play/pause, skip, and shuffle
•Tap the record on the now bar to open the album that song is in, scrolled to it with the row highlighted — no hunting through playlists
•Plays are counted honestly: a play only counts after you pass the halfway point of a track (or it plays to the end). Skipping through songs doesn't inflate your stats
•Tap the ⋮ (kebab) next to a song for more options — add to playlist, play next, delete, and more
Customizing the look
•Open Settings (gear icon) → Theme to pick a look
•Under Settings → Glow, mix and match edge lines, blur bands, and corner glow — all independent toggles, all customizable
•Settings → Playback has crossfade, gapless mode, and normalization
•Settings → Equalizer has 8 adjustable bands plus presets
Common scenarios, step by step
1 · Get one song off Spotify into SideCut (free)
In Spotify, open the song → Share → Copy link. In SideCut: Discover → paste it in the box under “Expand URL” → Expand, then copy the full link it shows you. Paste that into any Spotify-to-MP3 converter and download the file. Back in SideCut: + Add songs ▾ → + Files and pick the MP3. It's on your device now, and it plays offline forever.
2 · Make your own album from songs in different playlists
Open any list, long-press a row to enter select mode, tap every song you want (they can come from different playlists — select, add, then select again). Tap the album+ button in the header to make a new album, or the album-with-arrow to file them into an album you already made. Albums are yours to rename, reorder and export; nothing files itself in there automatically.
3 · Reorder songs in an album without misfiring
Open the album, then hold a song row for three seconds — a fill runs along the row so you can see the hold registering, and letting go early just plays the song. In the sheet that opens, drag the ≡ handles, or switch to another album with the chips at the bottom. Done keeps the new order, Cancel puts it back exactly as it was.
4 · Jump back to the song that's playing
Tap the record player on the now bar and SideCut takes you to whatever is playing, in the half of the library you are in. In Playlists it scrolls to that song in the list and tints the row (it switches to All Songs only when the playlist you have open does not contain it). In Albums it opens the album the song belongs to, scrolled to the row and highlighted — and if the song isn't in an album of yours yet, its album tag becomes a real album when you tap, so that jump never lands on an empty screen.
5 · Back everything up, or move to a new phone
+ Add songs ▾ → Export everything writes one .zip with your songs, covers, playlists, albums, tags and stats (a 500-song library takes 2–3 minutes; keep playing while it runs). On the new phone: + Add songs ▾ → Import library and pick that .zip. “Export songs only” is the smaller version with just the audio files.
6 · Keep SideCut up to date without digging for it
You don't have to check anything: when a new build is published, SideCut says so on the next launch and leaves an ⬆ Update available entry in the 🔔 bell with an Install now button. Installing never cuts a song — if music is playing it finishes what you asked for and applies the update when you leave the app. The manual way is still there: Settings → More → Check for updates.
Playlists & organizing
•Create playlists from the Playlists tab, then add songs via the kebab menu on any track
•Long-press a song row to select multiple tracks at once
•Albums hold the albums you made — the Albums tab shows only those, and the “Add to album” picker offers only those. Ones the app created for itself (an old auto-save, or a tag album from a reorder) stay out of the way under Manage albums
•Export library anytime to back everything up as a .zip you can restore later
